name: an editor adds to the catalog, a reader's addition becomes a request
an editor deletes what her person created, and asks to delete the rest
note: D45. 'Created' means the create change came from a device of the same person, whichever device it was.

name: only an administrator changes roles
an administrator promotes a reader to editor and lets him share
a demotion counts from its moment, whatever the order things arrive in
note: Laura's phone was offline and never saw the demotion. Her change from before it stands; the one after it becomes a request. Every delivery order must end the same, so a device that receives the demotion late re-evaluates the library from its log.

name: a device that belongs to no person acts as a reader
An unsigned operation is refused, with or without roles
note: D56: every operation is signed. 'unsigned' marks an operation without a signature; every other operation here is assumed correctly signed by the device in its hlc. A refused operation is not stored: it is neither applied nor a request.

name: an operation is all or nothing
note: The phone may edit Tersoal's tag but not delete it, so neither change is applied: the whole operation becomes one request.

name: a device renames itself, but only an administrator says whose it is
only an administrator resolves a request, and accepting applies it
note: Hugo, a reader, asks to add a publisher. Laura, an editor, cannot reject it: her attempt becomes a request too. Tersoal, the administrator, accepts it in an operation that also makes the change, signed by him.

name: whoever asked withdraws a request, and nobody else does
note: Hugo, a reader, asks to add a publisher with a note, carried as a change_request row inside the request. Laura, an editor, cannot withdraw Hugo's request: her attempt becomes a request. Hugo withdraws it himself.

name: each person keeps their own marks, whatever their role, and only theirs
note: A reader marks what he read and an editor what she is reading without asking. Changing someone else's mark is for administrators; a device of nobody marks nothing.

name: an operation dated inside the window of a fence becomes a request
note: Laura's phone signs an edit dated between the last operation the administrator had (trusted_through) and the demotion that carries the mark, chained to it. Whatever the order, it is a request: the HLC is the author's word, the fence is the administrator's (D84, D87).

name: an operation dated before the mark of a fence stays applied
note: Everything up to the mark was known to the administrator when the person was demoted, so the fence does not touch it, even if it arrives afterwards.

name: an operation dated below the mark and chained to an older one is a request (SEG-018)
note: Laura is demoted and the fence names her latest operation the administrator had. With a modified app her phone signs a new edit dated below that operation and chained to an older one of hers: a fork. It is not the marked operation nor one of its ancestors, so in any order it is a request. The edit made before the mark and the marked one stay applied.

name: after a fence the person is a reader and the fence changes nothing about that
note: Laura's edit after the demotion is a request, as it is without fences; her edit before it stays applied.

name: a fence set by someone who is not an administrator is ignored
note: Laura (editor) writes a fence on Hugo's tablet. Only administrators touch another device, so her operation is a request and the fence does not count: Hugo's edit dated inside that window stays applied, in every order.

name: a second fence does not reopen the window of the first
note: Laura is demoted, promoted again and demoted again. The device keeps only its latest trusted_through, but the first window comes from the log: the edit dated inside it stays a request.

name: a revoked device writes nothing after its revocation, even without roles
note: D71, D84 (SEG-015): what the device signs after a revocation still in force becomes a request, whichever device passes it on and in whatever order it arrives. What it signed before stays.

name: a device changes only its own device row, whatever its role

fields.name: Renamed by a device of nobody

name: an operation that becomes a request fences nobody, even next to a change that would be allowed
two devices of one person are one person for deleting what that person created
the key of a device counts only through its own create, and a registered one never changes
a fence on another device, without the author's own, is a plain fence and not a seal
note: The administrator fences Laura's phone with no change for her own device. It is the old fence: only the phone's operations dated inside its window are requests; a third device's operation dated before it stays applied.

name: the cloud says a person has an account and links a device of nobody to her, and that device gets her role
note: The cloud device, named by the administrator, writes account_id on Laura and then points a device of nobody at her. Both are applied and the device has Laura's role from then on: its edit afterwards is applied, in any order (D76).

fields.name: Added by the newly linked device

name: the cloud links a device of nobody to a person without an account, and that is a request
note: Hugo has no account_id. The cloud's link is a request, and the device stays a device of nobody: its edit is a request too.

name: the cloud does not reassign a device that already belongs to somebody
note: Hugo's phone is Hugo's. The cloud, with Laura's account written, points it at Laura: a request, and the phone stays Hugo's (a reader).

name: the cloud does not take a device's person away
note: The cloud empties the member_id of Hugo's phone: a request, and the phone stays Hugo's.

name: the cloud does not change roles
note: The cloud promotes Hugo to administrator, and separately changes his can_share: both are requests.

name: the cloud does not set a fence, alone or beside a link it could make
note: With Laura's account written, the cloud fences the device of nobody; then it fences it in the same operation that links it to Laura. Both are requests, and the device stays nobody's.

name: the cloud does not touch the catalog
note: The cloud creates a publisher: a request.

name: a device that is not the cloud cannot write account_id nor link a device
note: The cloud writes Laura's account. Then Hugo's phone writes Hugo's account and links the device of nobody to Laura; the device of nobody writes an account and links itself to Laura. All four are requests.

name: account_id is written by the cloud alone: not by a reader, not by an administrator, not at creation
note: A reader and an administrator each write an account_id, and the administrator creates a person with one already filled: three requests.

name: a reader who names himself the cloud gets nothing from it
note: Hugo's phone writes itself into library.cloud_device_id, then writes the administrator's account_id and links itself to her: three requests, because a reader may not change the library row.

name: the cloud's power ends with the operation that withdraws it, and the fence leaves what the administrator knew
note: The cloud writes Hugo's account and links a device of nobody to him; the administrator knows both. She then empties library.cloud_device_id with the fence of the cloud device marked at the link. The cloud's later link is a request (no power), and so is one it dated before but outside the chain (backdated).

name: another cloud: the power goes with the id the administrator names, each device by the date of its operation
note: The administrator names F, whose id does not derive from its key, then C, then F again. C writes at t30 (before it is named: request), at t45 and t46 (named: applied), and at t65 (named F again: request). F writes at t50 and has nothing at any time, because its id is not the one its key gives.

name: an emptied account_id stops new links, and leaves the devices already linked
note: The cloud links a device to Laura, then empties her account_id. A second device it links to her afterwards is a request; the first keeps her role.

name: the cloud's operation is all or nothing: one change it may not make turns the whole into a request
note: With the cloud named, one operation writes Laura's account (allowed) and changes Hugo's role (not allowed): a request, and Laura's account stays unwritten, so the link that needs it is a request too.

name: a device whose id does not derive from its registered key has no cloud power, even named
note: The administrator names F, registered with the test key but under an id that is not the one that key gives. F does what the cloud does in case 1: writes Laura's account, links a device of nobody to her, and the device acts. All requests.

name: the cloud device registers in an operation of its own: one that registers and writes account_id at once is a request
note: The administrator names the id that derives from the test key, but that device is not registered yet. Its first operation registers it and writes Laura's account in the same operation: judged before the registration, it has no power, so it is a request.

name: an administrator vouches for the real key of a device, and what it does afterwards is applied (D96)
a device assigned with another key is nobody's: what it does is a request, and so is its mark (D96)
a device assigned to an administrator with another key cannot change a role (D96, the attack)
an assignment without a vouched key, from before D96, still counts
only an administrator writes vouched_key: not a reader, not an editor, not on its own device
an administrator corrects the key: what is dated between the two assignments is a request, what comes after is applied
the assignment of a key arrives before the registration of the device and the verdict is the same (real key)
the assignment of a key arrives before the registration of the device and the verdict is the same (another key)
the cloud links a device with member_id alone: a request, and the device stays nobody's (D96, 7.5.3)
the cloud links a device vouching for the key it is registered with: applied, and the device has its person's role (D96, 7.5.3)
the cloud links a device vouching for another key: applied, but the device is nobody's (D96, 7.5.3)
the cloud writes vouched_key alone, on a device of nobody or one that belongs to somebody: a request (7.5.3)
withdrawing a person's access, with their device left without a person, fenced and revoked: what the device signs after is a request (D98)
the mark alone, without touching the device: the device still points at the person but what it signs after is a request (D98)
what the expelled signs dated before the withdrawal and unknown to the administrator is a request; the marked one and its ancestors stay applied (D98)
only whoever may write role writes access_withdrawn: not an editor, not a reader, not the expelled to take it off (D98)
the cloud links a new device to a person whose access was withdrawn: a request; to one who has it: applied (D98)
the administrator gives the access back and links the device again: what comes after is applied, what came between is a request (D98)
an administrator whose access was withdrawn can no longer change roles (D98)
an author written in capitals is not read, so the cloud's id in capitals gets none of its power (SEG-029)
deleting a person is for administrators, even when the editor who deletes her created her (SEG-034)
an editor deletes a person she created and nobody else touched: still a request (SEG-034)
FOUNDING: a library is founded by the key its id derives from, and a device that was not given a place writes nothing
note: The founding creates the library, its first person as an administrator and the founding device's place in one operation. The id of the library derives from the key of that device and the nonce (rule 1). Another device that registers itself and writes without anybody saying whose it is, is a device of nobody: a reader.

name: FOUNDING: a founding with a nonce the id does not derive from founds nothing
note: The library id derives from the key and the nonce N; the operation carries another nonce. It is a request, nobody has a role, and nothing the founder writes afterwards is allowed.

name: FOUNDING: a founding dated before the real one, by a device the id does not derive from, takes nothing
note: Mallory's device signs a founding dated before the true one and makes an administrator of itself. The id of the library does not derive from what it carries, so it is a request in every order of arrival, and the true founding stands (D97; the seal of D94 is gone).

name: FOUNDING: the nonce never changes, not even for an administrator
note: An operation that touches `founding_nonce` outside the founding is a request as a whole, its rename included; the next operation of the administrator is allowed.

name: FOUNDING: a library is founded once: the same key founding it again is a request
note: Once somebody has a role, the library is founded. A second founding, even by the founder with the same nonce, is judged like any operation and it writes `founding_nonce`: a request.

name: FOUNDING: what a device writes before the library is founded is a request, even the founder's
note: Before the founding nobody has a role, and that means nobody may write (there is no longer a mode where everybody may). Registering one's own device is the only thing allowed. The founder's own operation dated before it is a request, in every order.

name: FOUNDING: an unsigned founding is refused
note: Every operation is signed (D56), the founding too.

name: a person who is not an administrator leaves the library from one device, cutting off her own devices: the mark, no person, the withdrawal of each, and a fence only on the signing one (D102)
a reader leaves the library too: her device is cut off and what it signs afterwards is a request (D102)
an exit that asks for more than leaving is a request as a whole: another person's device, a book, a role, no mark, another person's mark, a fence on another device, a wrong fence (D102)
an exit signed by a device of nobody, by one with the wrong vouched key, or that names another person, is a request (D102)
a person who has left cannot take the mark off herself, and the administrator can (D102, D98)
